You'll now see some of my links tagged with "Not Encrypted." Let me try to describe what that means, and someone feel free to correct me on this.

Generally speaking an "encrypted" exchange of information is a secure one. Websites provide "a certificate" which includes said encryption (anyone who has customized a Wordpress site knows about certificates). When you send information to websites (i.e. link to them, input passwords, interact with them, etc), the info is encrypted at your computer and then decrypted at the website.

Usually, the information cannot be read or tampered with in transit. However, if a website is not encrypted, or if a hacker can decode the encryption, you might be at risk of an MITM attack. This means that any of my links that read "Not Encrypted" should be visited carefully, especially when you're browsing publicly (at Starbucks, library, etc).

Oddly enough, the most reputable sources I link to (AL.com, SB Nation, ESPN) are tagged as "Not Encrypted," and all three are highly trafficked media outlets. All that being said, consider these tags as a "heads up" more than a strict warning, since I've never been compromised when visiting them.
